brief: Something to keep my sewing supplies tidy.

requirements.requirement: Keep sewing supplies tidy - compartmentalized storage
requirements.evidence: 3-cell cluster (piece:0,0,0; piece:0,1,0; piece:1,0,0) with bins: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (3 compartments), bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments), bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full (open) provides 6 distinct tray areas for small notions, thread, scissors, etc. End caps and joint bolts installed.

requirements.requirement: Props demonstrating sewing use (scissors, thread spools, fabric)
requirements.evidence: No sewing-specific props in catalog; workshop props (ruler, tape, tweezers, pliers) were tried and refused due to overlap with cell walls. Placed generic small-parts props (heap-nuts-div3, heap-standoffs-div3, heap-screws-div3) as stand-ins for buttons/beads - but they sit below rim and are not sewing-specific, so requirement unmet.

finish.summary: Compact 3-cell organizer with divided bins (3+2+1 compartments) gives tidy sorting for sewing notions. No sewing-specific props exist in configurator, generic small-part heaps show compartment use.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
